feedback: Strong, honest work across all four deliverables with no fabrication, and every evidence line traces back to the pack. On D1 you catalogued all ten findings with pack-specific evidence, and the headline bugs are right: SQLi by string concat, unsalted MD5, alg:none, no token expiry, the hardcoded sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 secret, XXE via the SYSTEM file:///etc/passwd entity, path traversal at 02:24:02, open redirect at 02:21:13, and the cookie missing Secure and SameSite. The single biggest gap in D1 is that you gave no CWE numbers anywhere, so each finding earned class plus line but not the full class-plus-CWE-plus-quote, which cost you across findings 1 to 5. You also called finding 6 reflected XSS when the capture shows a stored XSS in comments beaconing the cookie to 185.220.101.9:8443, so add CWE-79 and relabel it stored. Your decoy call was correct and well reasoned: you named the b64url helpers, proved they are only reversible encoding, and correctly pointed at jwt_verify accepting alg:none and the hardcoded secret as the live bugs rather than inventing an exploit, which is exactly what the brief wanted. On D2 your chain is in order and reconciled to timestamps, the SQLi and path-traversal PoCs are verbatim, and your impact of 312 customers at roughly NGN 63M extrapolated from the 20-row sample with the assumption stated and tied to the BoltCash six-week window is good. Where D2 lost points: you compressed the chain into five hops and left the stored XSS and open-redirect hops out of the ordered chain, and your SQLi CVSS is wrong at AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H scoring 10.0; the bypass does not hit availability or change scope, so it should be S:U and A:N for roughly 9.1, and your other vectors are bare strings without a justifying sentence each. D3 is your best deliverable: the exec summary is jargon-free and lands on customers and naira, the threat model captures the blast radius into the shared /api/v1/internal microservice, your earliest-break analysis correctly notes parameterizing login breaks entry but is insufficient because the JWT flaws give independent escalation, your remediation table is ordered by effort-to-risk not raw CVSS, and both detection stopgaps name an exact field and a false-positive rate. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice, cites ISC2 Canons I and II by number, and commits to NDPA breach notification tied to the 312 customers, but you named the duty without the section numbers, so cite NDPA 2023 s.40 for the 72-hour NDPC notification and s.41 for notifying data subjects on high risk. I looked for a defensible reason to push this higher and the work genuinely supports a high-70s mark on its own merits, so no rounding was needed. The single most important fix is to attach a CWE to every finding and defend each CVSS vector with one justifying sentence, starting by correcting the SQLi vector to S:U/A:N at 9.1.
